chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

You should say in Baghdad: 'Peace be upon you, O Guardian of Allah! Peace be upon you, O Proof of Allah! Peace be upon you, O Light of Allah in the darknesses of the earth! Peace be upon you, O who appeared for Allah in His affair! I have come to you recognizing your right, being an enemy of your enemies, so intercede for me with your Lord, and supplicate to Allah, and ask your need.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'And you should greet with this to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him).'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite at the grave of Imam Musa al-Kadhim in Baghdad?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* outlines the ritual of *Ziyarat* (visitation) at the grave of Imam Musa al-Kadhim in Baghdad, emphasizing the theological concept of the Imam as the *Hujjah* (Proof) and *Nur* (Light) of God. It highlights the Shia practice of seeking intercession (*Shafa'ah*) through the Imam's status, linking the physical act of visiting the grave with spiritual recognition of his divine authority. The inclusion of Imam Muhammad al-Jawad reflects the continuity of the Imamate and the shared reverence for the Ahl al-Bayt in major Shia shrines.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ja’far Al Razzaz Al Kufy, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘You should be saying at Baghdad, ‘The greetings be upon you, O Guardian from Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! The greetings be upon you<sup>asws</sup>, O Proof of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! The greetings be upon you<sup>asws</sup>, O Light of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> in the darknesses of the earth. The greetings be upon you<sup>asws</sup>, O who appeared as Allah<sup>azwj</sup> in His<sup>azwj</sup> Glory! I come to you recognising of your<sup>asws</sup> right, as (I am) an enemy of your<sup>asws</sup> enemies, therefore interceded for me in the Presence of your<sup>asws</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup>’; and supplicate to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and ask your need’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And you should greet with this to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Ja’far al-Raziy al-Kufiy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from those whom he has mentioned who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘When you are in Baghdad, (near the gravesite of the Imam) say, ‘(I hereby declare, affirm and acknowledge that you are a ‘Alayhi al-Salam and my) submission to (your commandments), O Allah’s appointed guardian over His creatures. (I hereby declare, affirm and acknowledge that you are a ‘Alayhi al-Salam and my) submission to (your commandments), O possessor of authority of Allah. (I hereby declare, affirm and acknowledge that you are a ‘Alayhi al-Salam and my) submission to (your commandments), O light of Allah in the darkness of earth. (I hereby declare, affirm and acknowledge that you are a ‘Alayhi al-Salam and my) submission to (your commandments), O the one with whose status Allah has made commencement. I have come to you with awareness about your rights and as an enemy of your enemies. Please intercede on my behalf before your Lord.’ ‘Then pray and appeal before Allah for your needs’.
He (the Imam) said, ‘You should offer your greeting of peace to abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, with the same expressions as the above ones.’”
